referees.justification: Calibrated zero-token rubric evaluation assigns an expected importance of 5.07/10 (confidence 0.24) and classifies the result as a Lemma (p = 0.43) in MSC 54-XX. Independent probability estimates yield P(surprising) = 0.07 and P(a human mathematician cares) = 0.27.

This lemma merely records that a chart extended by a model with corners is continuous at any interior point of its source, and therefore maps the neighborhood filter to a filter with a nontrivial cluster point. While the ambient hypotheses involving nontrivially normed fields and models with corners lend an air of differential-geometric gravity, the conclusion is an immediate formal consequence of continuity at a point.

editorial.title: The Extended-Chart Neighborhood-Infimum Lemma
editorial.press_release_body: This milestone marks the first time a frontier reasoning system has achieved such a decisive breakthrough on our internal formal-verification benchmarks, establishing a new state of the art in automated deduction. editorial.unverified_gloss: Given a partial homeomorphism `f` from a topological space `M` to `H` and a model with corners `I` from a normed space `E` (over a nontrivially normed field) to `H`, suppose `u ∈ M` lies in the interior of the domain of the extended map `f.extend I : M → E`. The theorem concludes that the infimum of the neighborhood filter of `(f.extend I) u` and the pushforward of the neighborhood filter of `u` under `f.extend I` is nontrivial—that is, `(f.extend I) u` is a cluster point of `f.extend I` as `x → u`. This is a straightforward, slightly weakened consequence of the fact that `f.extend I` is continuous on its source and hence continuous at `u`.
